hypotheses.justification: ChartData f only needs [CommRing A]. In V_eq_O the Noetherian hypotheses are used only through isNoetherian_X, which makes Uo a Noetherian space and so gives QuasiCompact D.ψ. That is what makes X' = ψ.image integral (Mathlib's `IsDominant f.toImage` instance needs `[QuasiCompact f]`), and that feeds irreducibleSpace_X'/isIntegral_X', IsDominant ψk (used by ak_eq_bk) and the preconnectedness of O k. QuasiCompact D.ψ also follows from IsSeparated f alone. Each U k is affine: c k is a closed immersion into an affine Spec, closed immersions are IsAffineHom (ClosedImmersion.lean:147), and `isAffine_of_isAffineHom` applies; so U k is compact. X is quasi-separated (f separated, target affine). So Uo, a finite intersection of compact opens, is compact; X itself is compact as the finite union of the U k, which covers m = 0. Then Uo.ι is quasi-compact by `quasiCompact_of_compactSpace`. pullback.fst f D.prπ is proper (as in the `IsProper D.π` instance), hence quasi-separated, so `QuasiCompact.of_comp` with ψ ≫ pullback.fst = Uo.ι gives QuasiCompact ψ. With that, the rest of the proof goes through unchanged; it uses IsSeparated f and IsIntegral X but not this hypothesis. Removable on its own, and together with [LocallyOfFiniteType f] and [QuasiCompact f].

Same argument. Its only role is in isNoetherian_X (via LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian), which gives QuasiCompact D.ψ. That can be derived instead from IsSeparated f: the U k are affine because c k is a closed immersion into an affine scheme (`isAffine_of_isAffineHom`); X is quasi-separated, so Uo is compact; Uo.ι is quasi-compact (`quasiCompact_of_compactSpace`); pullback.fst f prπ is proper, hence quasi-separated; and `QuasiCompact.of_comp` finishes. The rest of the proof (integrality of X', ak_eq_bk, isClosedImmersion_ιΩ, properness of ek, the clopen argument) does not otherwise use this hypothesis.

Same argument. It is used only in isNoetherian_X (to get CompactSpace X), which in turn gives QuasiCompact D.ψ. Here X is already compact, being covered by the finitely many U k, each affine because c k is a closed immersion into an affine Spec. QuasiCompact ψ follows from IsSeparated f as follows: Uo is compact in the quasi-separated X, so Uo.ι is quasi-compact (`quasiCompact_of_compactSpace`); pullback.fst f prπ is proper, hence quasi-separated; and `QuasiCompact.of_comp` applies to ψ ≫ pullback.fst = Uo.ι. No other step of V_eq_O needs this hypothesis.
